title: Chapter 146: Livestream Time Confirmed
html:
Wang Shenglong’s smile was gone. He erased the words, pain flashing through his small eyes.

“We have both become monsters?” Chen Ge struck the door, pain radiating through his back.

Hearing the commotion in the bedroom, Doctor Gao and Wang Shenglong’s family ran in. “Chen Ge, what happened?”

“I slipped and hit the door.” Chen Ge rubbed his back and stood.

“Are you hurt? I have ointment.” Shenglong’s father accepted the excuse and went to search. Doctor Gao, however, glanced at the undisturbed carpet and said nothing.

“I’m fine. It isn’t serious.” With Doctor Gao’s help, Chen Ge left the bedroom. The visit had not gone as hoped. Shenglong’s apparent cooperation was a performance designed to conceal the true cause of his condition.

Why hide it? Is something forcing him?Helplessness and pain had filled Shenglong’s face, yet he seemed unwilling to change. Rolling his sore shoulder, Chen Ge realized the man was stronger than most adults.

He looks harmless, but he is dangerous.Chen Ge could not force the truth from him in front of his family—and even alone, he was not confident he could overpower Shenglong.

Chen Ge suggested they leave so he could privately ask Doctor Gao about Shenglong’s secret. As the father escorted them out and exchanged contact information, Chen Ge glimpsed the devastated Shenglong lifting his board again.

As if aware of Chen Ge’s gaze, he drew quickly and turned the board toward the doorway.

What does it mean?Several figures sat inside a house. A monster stood on the smallest one’s shoulders, bent low as it surveyed the others, ready to leap onto them.

Is he warning me?Chen Ge memorized the picture, then accompanied Doctor Gao downstairs to collect Men Nan’s belongings from Room 304.

After closing the door and confirming the brothers had not followed, Chen Ge asked, “Doctor Gao, how serious is Wang Shenglong’s condition?”

“Something is abnormal.” Doctor Gao rolled Men Nan’s sheets and pillows inside a quilt. “His father describes a serious condition, yet my initial assessment found clear, logical thought and a willingness to communicate. That conflicts with his vacant smile. A healthy person can control their expression. He is intelligent and skilled at hiding emotion—but the performance is too deliberate. He is concealing something.”

Chen Ge was impressed. “You are the professional. But if you noticed, why not tell his father? Wouldn’t that help treatment?”

“Managing a patient’s family requires care. Shenglong’s father welcomed us today, but if his son felt threatened, he would take Shenglong’s side and deny us future access.” Doctor Gao lifted the bundle. “Help me pack the books and notes from Men Nan’s drawer. They matter greatly to him.”

Chen Ge emptied the drawer book by book. At the bottom lay a photograph of a woman in a hospital gown with a shy boy seated beside her.

“Men Nan and his mother?” Even without makeup, the woman was strikingly beautiful. “His father cheated despite having such a beautiful wife.”

Since the first love letter Chen Ge ever received came from a Baleful Specter, his understanding of romance was limited. Still, something seemed wrong with Men Nan’s father. He slipped the photograph into a book, packed the box, and left with Doctor Gao.

Outside Hai Ming Apartments, Chen Ge drew a deep breath. “Finally, fresh air.”

“Stench? It smells worse out here.” Doctor Gao pointed to rubbish piled like a small hill.

“Didn’t you smell a weird stench in Wang Shenglong’s room?”

“No. Their apartment is clean, and his father cares for him well.” Doctor Gao sighed. “In that respect, Shenglong is fortunate. His entire family supports his recovery.”

“They truly care.” The family’s concern could not be faked. After several steps, Chen Ge stopped. “Family?”

“Yes. Some families abandon patients at rehabilitation centers.” Doctor Gao misunderstood. Chen Ge was thinking of the drawing. The smallest figure was Shenglong; the people around him were his family. The monster looked ready to jump onto them. Was Shenglong refusing treatment because any resistance would endanger those he loved?

The drawing also proved that after all these years, the towering monster still stood on his shoulders, and their game had never ended.

“The odor comes from the monster, but why can only I smell it?” Each answer produced more questions. Only entering the Third Sick Hall would resolve them. After loading Men Nan’s belongings, Doctor Gao drove Chen Ge back to New Century Park.

The moment Chen Ge stepped from the car, Liu Dao called. “Brother, Qin Guang announced his next livestream. It’s tomorrow night.”

“So soon? Then do you know where the location will be?”

“Mu Yang High School.” The familiar name made Chen Ge pause. Liu Dao continued, “This time, Qin Guang hired a writer to adapt your stream into a script. Legally, he can call it an homage rather than plagiarism, so the platform can’t act.”

Chen Ge’s long silence made Liu Dao assume he was angry. “Some things are beyond our control, but hard work will win in the end.”

“That isn’t it. If you get the chance, send Qin Guang a message for me.”

“What message?”

Chen Ge looked at the Haunted House in the darkness. “Tell him to stop following me. If he continues, I can’t guarantee his safety.”
